obligation: NRC cyber security event notification: adverse impact
trigger: Cyberattack that adversely impacted safety-related, important-to-safety, security, or EP functions (including offsite communications), or compromised support systems with such impacts
deadline: Within 1 hour after discovery
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center via ENS (commercial line if ENS is unavailable, 73.77(c)(1))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - not expected from a business network attack because Levels 3 and 4 are isolated; applies if the CST finds any impact on a CDA

obligation: NRC cyber security event notification: could have impacted
trigger: Cyberattack that could have caused an adverse impact to those functions, or could have compromised support systems (for example, an attacker on the business network probing the receive server or a vendor path to CDAs)
deadline: Within 4 hours after discovery
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center via ENS
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the main NRC clock for this runbook. The Shift Manager decides with the CST; IT supplies facts

obligation: NRC cyber security event notification: insider-initiated
trigger: Suspected or actual cyberattack initiated by personnel with physical or electronic access to systems within 73.54 scope
deadline: Within 4 hours after discovery
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center via ENS
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - main clock for the insider runbook
owner: Shift Manager (with the Director of Security and the CST)

obligation: NRC cyber security event notification: after notifying another agency
trigger: Notification to a local, State, or other Federal agency (for example the FBI) of an event related to the cyber security program that does not otherwise require 73.77 notification
deadline: Within 4 hours after the notification to the other agency
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center via ENS
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - this is why no one reports to the FBI, CISA, or the E-ISAC before the Shift Manager is told (POL-03 4.5)
clock_starts: Time of the report to the other agency

obligation: NRC cyber security event notification: intelligence gathering
trigger: Information about observed behavior, activities, or statements that may indicate intelligence gathering or pre-operational planning related to a cyberattack against systems in 73.54 scope (for example reconnaissance aimed at the Station seen by the MSSP)
deadline: Within 8 hours after receipt or collection of the information
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center via ENS
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
clock_starts: Receipt or collection of the information

obligation: Corrective action program recording
trigger: Vulnerabilities, weaknesses, failures, and deficiencies in the 73.54 program; and any notification made under 73.77(a)
deadline: Within 24 hours of discovery
notify: Site corrective action program (internal record); paper CAP intake form if CAP is down (POL-03 4.6)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Written security follow-up report
trigger: Telephonic notification made under 73.77(a)(1), (a)(2)(i), or (a)(2)(ii)
deadline: Within 60 days of the telephonic notification, on NRC Form 366; keep a copy 3 years or until license termination, whichever comes first
notify: NRC (addresses in 73.4) plus a copy to the Director, Office of Nuclear Security and Incident Response
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - not required after (a)(2)(iii) or (a)(3) notifications

obligation: Notifications containing SGI
trigger: A notification that must include SGI or classified information
deadline: Within the same 73.77 timeframe
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center by secure telephone; if secure communication is unavailable, give what is required without SGI and say so
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Events also reportable under 50.72 or 50.73
trigger: A cyber event that also requires an emergency declaration or a 50.72 or 50.73 report (for example a cyber cause found later for a plant event)
deadline: As set by 50.72 or 50.73 (not restated here); separate 73.77 notifications are not required, but the notification should also indicate the 73.77 criteria
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - unlikely from a business network event

obligation: NRC physical security event: report to law enforcement
trigger: An event related to the security program (for example suspected theft or disclosure of SGI or physical security information by an insider) for which a notification was made to local, State, or Federal law enforcement, and that does not otherwise require a 73.1200 notification
deadline: Within 4 hours (73.1200(e) four-hour category); no written follow-up report is required for (e) notifications about law enforcement interactions
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - insider runbook. Calling the FBI or local police about an SGI or physical security matter starts this clock, just as a cyber event report starts the 73.77(a)(2)(iii) clock
owner: Shift Manager (with the Director of Security)

obligation: NRC physical security event: previously unrecognized vulnerability
trigger: Identification or discovery of a previously unrecognized vulnerability that could prevent implementation of the protective strategy for protecting any target set (for example if compromised SGI reveals one)
deadline: Within 4 hours after time of discovery; written follow-up report within 60 days (73.1205(a)(1))
applies_at_this_tier: Possible - the Director of Security assesses what the compromised SGI reveals
owner: Shift Manager (with the Director of Security)

obligation: Suspicious activity report
trigger: Activity the company assesses as suspicious, such as elicitation of non-public information about the security or emergency response programs from company or contractor personnel
deadline: Assessment and reports as soon as possible but within 4 hours of discovery
notify: In this order: local law enforcement agency, FBI local field office, NRC Headquarters Operations Center
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - insider runbook variant C (outsider seeking SRI or SGI from staff). Not also required if a 73.1200 notification is made (73.1215(c)(1)(ii))
owner: Director of Security (Shift Manager makes the NRC call)

obligation: Physical security event recording
trigger: A threatened, attempted, or committed act that has resulted in or could decrease the effectiveness of the physical security program below the NRC-approved physical security plan, not reported under 73.1200
deadline: Record within 24 hours of discovery; keep 3 years after the last entry or until license termination, whichever is later
notify: Safeguards event log or CAP security entries (SGI kept out of the general CAP record, 73.1210(b)(3)(iii)-(iv))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SGI or physical security information compromise that does not meet a 73.1200 criterion

obligation: Access authorization: new adverse information
trigger: New or changed information with adverse implications for the trustworthiness and reliability of an individual who holds unescorted access or unescorted access authorization under another licensee program (for example an outage contractor)
deadline: On the day of discovery
notify: Reviewing official of each other licensee program under which the individual holds unescorted access status
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - insider runbook
owner: Director of Security (access authorization reviewing official)

obligation: NERC low-impact Reportable Cyber Security Incident
trigger: A Cyber Security Incident that is determined to be a Reportable Cyber Security Incident affecting a low-impact BES Cyber System (dispatch network)
deadline: Determination and notification under the company plan; the standard sets no fixed time for low impact. Company target: E-ISAC within 1 hour of determination, after the Shift Manager is told
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - only if the dispatch network (SYS-15) is affected
clock_starts: Determination that the incident is reportable
owner: Compliance and GRC Lead with the CIP Senior Manager

obligation: Balancing Authority coordination and Form DOE-417 support
citation: Form DOE-417 instructions (OMB 1901-0288), Who Must Submit; Balancing Authority agreement
trigger: Telemetry or dispatch disruption, or a cyber event that could affect the unit's availability
deadline: Company practice: call the Balancing Authority immediately on telemetry loss; give it the information it needs for its own reports
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, as support only. The company is not a DOE-417 filer: commercial power reactors subject to the Part 73 event notification rules are excluded from the Generating Entities respondent group
clock_starts: Telemetry loss or suspected cyber cause
owner: Energy Marketing and Settlements Manager with the Shift Manager

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (employee, contractor, or access authorization records)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (up to 15 more days for good cause if the Department is told in writing within the 30 days); law enforcement delay allowed
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if personal information was accessed (SYS-05, SYS-11, file shares)

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (the 15-day extension does not apply to this notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Floridians (the workforce and outage contractor records can exceed 500)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Possible (access authorization records cover about 2,000 people)

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company (ERP, background screening vendor) has a breach
deadline: Vendor must notify the company within 10 days after determining the breach
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contract amendments due 2027-03-31 (P03 G-081)

obligation: Other state breach notification
citation: State breach notification statutes in each state where affected individuals reside (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents of other states (outage contractors come from many states)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Affected residents; state regulators where required
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - check residency of every affected individual

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25. As proposed, the nuclear reactor sector criterion would cover the company. Review the final rule within 30 days of publication (P01 R-049)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); law enforcement
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
trigger: Confirmed intrusion, ransomware, or insider theft of security information
deadline: After the Shift Manager has been told (a report to another agency can start the 73.77(a)(2)(iii) 4-hour clock)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - recommended, through the decision point
clock_starts: Decision by the incident commander and General Counsel
owner: IT Security Manager through General Counsel

obligation: PPA-2 buyer notice
trigger: Security incident affecting the GDSR service or buyer data
deadline: Within 48 hours of confirmation (contract term)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual
owner: Energy Marketing and Settlements Manager with General Counsel

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier hotline before engaging incident vendors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: Private equity sponsor notice
trigger: Severity 1 incident
deadline: Within 24 hours (contract term)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05
trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at an SEC registrant
deadline: 4 business days after the materiality determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - privately held company

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky article discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: 52.204-25(d): within 1 business day, then 10 business days; 52.204-23(c): within 3 business days, then 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts
